newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's future lies with NAFTA and EU -- Cardoso.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's future lies with NAFTA and EU -- Cardoso.

text.p: Brazil will not seek to ally itself exclusively with either the North American Free Trade Agreement (NAFTA) or the European Union (EU), a spokesman for President Fernando Henrique Cardoso said.

"According to the president, Brazilian policy will not leave out the EU or NAFTA. Closer ties with both blocks are important," the spokesman said, refering to comments made by Cardoso in an interview with CNN television.
During an official visit to Brazil last week, French President Jacques Chirac proposed a 1998 summit to boost ties between Latin America and the EU.

Cardoso responded by saying the summit should be held in Rio de Janeiro. Brazil has traditionally viewed itself as a "global player" big enough to claim its own turf between the United States and European spheres of influence. It has resisted pressure, principally from Argentina, to line up behind the U.S. and NAFTA.
President Bill Clinton is due to visit Brazil in May with freer trade one of the hottest issues on his agenda.

But Cardoso told CNN he would not bring up "technical details like tariffs" with his U.S. counterpart and would instead discuss wider-ranging issues, in particular the need to improve education in Latin America, the spokesman said.
